title: Curried Roast Pumpkin Soup with Coconut and Thyme
summary: A smooth, gently spiced soup of roasted pumpkin blended with curry powder, ginger and coconut milk, finished with thyme, black pepper and a roasted pumpkin wedge.
equipment: 2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled, deseeded, in 4 cm chunks, plus 6 thin wedges to garnish
hot water or low-salt vegetable stock
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast the pumpkin
steps.text: Heat the oven to 210 °C (190 °C fan). Toss the chunks and garnish wedges with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of the salt, spread on the trays and roast 30-35 min until soft and browned at the edges. Keep the wedges aside.

steps.title: Cook the aromatics
steps.text: Meanwhile heat the rest of the oil in the saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 min until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 min, then the curry powder and cumin for 30 sec until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the roasted chunks, the water and the rest of the salt. Bring to the boil and simmer 10 min.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the coconut milk and warm through without boiling. Add the lime juice, then taste and adjust.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle into bowls, scatter with thyme leaves and black pepper and lay a roasted wedge alongside.

tips: Roasting the pumpkin first gives a sweeter, deeper flavour than boiling.
Fry the curry powder briefly in the oil so it loses its raw taste.
Do not boil the soup after adding the coconut milk.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
